turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hello. I suppose what made me come in is that my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. Some days I just forget lunch completely. I'll be sitting there watching out the front window—the Robinsons across the street just painted their front door this bright, awful red color, and I was watching the painters tape it off, wondering why on earth anyone would choose red for a brown brick house. It clashes terribly, don't you think? It's just an eyesore. 

But anyway... other days, I don't know, I just stand right at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets. Just standing there mindlessly. And the funny thing is, nothing even tastes right. I bought those little buttery crackers that were on sale at the grocery store on Tuesday, the ones in the yellow box, but they just taste like cardboard to me now. I don't know why I even buy them if they're just going to taste like that. The cashier there, the young girl with the glasses, she always bags my groceries too heavy anyway... but yes, my eating is just all out of sorts.

Speaking of rest, I actually bought one of those memory foam mattresses a while back to try and help with my sleep. Well, I say a while, it was probably around the time my sister's dog had that litter of puppies. Golden retrievers... oh, they were precious little things, but they chewed through absolutely everything. She had this beautiful antique rug in her front hallway, passed down from our mother, and one of those puppies just tore the fringe right off one side of it. My sister was beside herself. She tried to have it repaired, but the man at the carpet shop said the weave was too old to match the thread. It's a shame, really, how nice things just get ruined like that. 

But yes, the mattress... the salesman told me it would be wonderful for my lower back. He was a very tall man, kept adjusting his tie the whole time he talked to me. turns.patient_response:
Well, I suppose I do put off things that used to just be part of my normal routine. I actually stopped teaching my craft classes down at the community center because of it. We used to have such a lovely time. Last spring we were doing decoupage... taking those pretty paper napkins and pasting them onto glass jars to make lanterns. My friend Martha brought in these beautiful napkins with little hydrangeas on them. Hydrangeas are so temperamental to grow, though. I tried planting them in my front yard years ago, but the soil here is just too alkaline. They turned this muddy pink color instead of that brilliant blue. My neighbor told me you have to add coffee grounds to the dirt to get the blue, but my husband didn't drink coffee, only tea, so we never had any grounds. Lipton, usually, with just a little squeeze of lemon. 

Anyway, I haven't been back to teach in months. And I've been missing phone calls and appointments, and all sorts of family tasks I used to handle so carefully. Like my nephew's birthday... I completely forgot to call him. I remember when he was born, it was the hottest July on record. The hospital air conditioning broke down, and they had to bring in these massive yellow fans that sounded like airplane engines. It was miserable for his poor mother. 

But yes, I still manage to stay in my home, thankfully. I haven't had to move in with anyone. I just have to rely a lot more on reminders now... little sticky notes on the fridge and the counter, otherwise I just put everything off and nothing gets done.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever gotten lost or confused about where you were while walking or driving in familiar places, like your own neighborhood?
turns.patient_response: No, I can't say I've ever gotten lost like that. I've lived in this neighborhood for... oh, it must be forty years now. We bought the house right after the big blizzard of '78. I remember the snow was piled so high you couldn't even see the mailboxes. We had to shovel a path just to get to the street, and my husband's shovel actually snapped in half because the ice was so thick underneath. He had to borrow one from Mr. Henderson next door. Mr. Henderson was such a nice man, he used to grow the most enormous tomatoes I've ever seen. Beefsteaks, he called them. He'd bring us a basket every August, and I'd make these wonderful tomato sandwiches on white bread with just a little mayonnaise and salt. You can't get tomatoes that taste like that at the supermarket anymore. They always taste so mealy and watery, like they've been sitting in a refrigerator for weeks. I tried growing my own once, in a little pot on the back porch, but the squirrels got to them before they even turned red. Those squirrels just take one bite out of a green tomato and leave it sitting on the railing. It's so frustrating. But no, I always know my way around the streets here.
